name: Felaris
description: A smooth, lightweight modern browser built in Rust.

showcase.headline: Browse lighter. Stay in flow.
showcase.intro: Felaris is a fast, lightweight browser for Windows. Tabs live in a calm sidebar, Ctrl+T opens a floating search over the page, and tabs you aren't using go to sleep so your PC stays responsive.
features: Floating new-tab search across your tabs, history and shortcuts
Site controls for HTTPS security, permissions and clearing site data
Idle tabs sleep and playing tabs mute right from the sidebar

page.summary: Felaris is a Rust browser for Windows that keeps out of your way. A collapsible sidebar holds your tabs and workspaces, a floating search bar opens over whatever you're reading, and background tabs sleep automatically so memory goes to the page in front of you. The installer is about 3 MB.

sections.title: Everything within reach.
sections.intro: A sidebar instead of a tab strip, with the tools you reach for every day built in.

items.title: Zen-style sidebar
items.text: Tabs, pins and workspaces sit in a 260px sidebar that folds into a 56px rail with Ctrl+Shift+B. Drag tabs or press Alt+Shift+Up/Down to reorder them, click the speaker icon to mute a noisy tab, or right-click for quick actions.

items.title: Workspaces
items.text: Group tabs by task and switch with Alt+1 to 9. Workspaces organise tabs, not accounts, so your logins carry across them. Rename or delete workspaces from the picker without reloading live pages.

items.title: Private tabs
items.text: Ctrl+Shift+N opens a tab in the Private workspace. Its pages use an InPrivate profile, and none of their tabs, history or top sites are saved.

items.title: Ad blocking built in
items.text: uBlock Origin Lite is fetched on first launch, checked against a known hash, and loaded into every tab. Switch it off in Settings whenever you like.

items.title: Bookmarks & local suggestions
items.text: Press Ctrl+D to bookmark a page. The address bar and floating search suggest open tabs, bookmarks, history and shortcuts with site favicons, without sending autocomplete queries to the network.

items.title: Session recovery
items.text: Tabs, workspaces, pins and recently closed tabs are saved locally with a backup, so they come back after a restart.

sections.title: Built to stay light.
sections.intro: Felaris keeps about twelve pages awake and lets the rest rest, without losing the work you care about.

items.title: Automatic tab sleeping
items.text: Older background tabs unload once you have about twelve live pages. Pinned tabs, active downloads, playing media and pages with unsaved edits stay awake.

items.title: Sleep on demand & tab mute
items.text: Press Ctrl+Shift+S to unload background tabs right away. Selecting a sleeping tab reloads it from its saved address, and muted tabs keep their mute state across sleep and restarts.

items.title: Floating sign-in windows
items.text: Login and OAuth popups open in a floating window that shares your session, with a one-click option to turn it into a full tab.

items.title: Native downloads
items.text: Downloads show progress and file actions, empty download-only tabs close themselves automatically, and Felaris warns you before closing while a transfer is still running.

items.title: Site controls & permissions
items.text: Click the lock or warning icon in the address bar to inspect the site’s origin and HTTPS status or clear its cookies and stored data. Permission choices are remembered in your profile across visits.

items.title: Ready to be your default
items.text: Felaris registers for web links and HTML files. Pick it from the sidebar menu and Windows keeps the final choice with you.

sections.title: Keep your hands on the keys.
sections.intro: Shortcuts work even when a page has focus, so sites can’t swallow them.

rows: Focus the address and search bar
Reorder a focused tab within its group

requirements: Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime, included with Windows
Installs for the current user, without an administrator prompt
page.note: Sleeping tabs reload their saved address when you return to them, so unsaved form input does not survive sleep or a restart. Pin a tab to keep it awake.

name: SpeakFlow
description: Local and cloud speech-to-text for Windows.

showcase.headline: Speak naturally. Keep your flow.
showcase.intro: Hold a hotkey, speak, then release. SpeakFlow turns your words into text in the app you're already using, with local and cloud recognition options.
features: Choose local or cloud speech recognition
showcase.imageAlt: SpeakFlow's dark dictation workspace with recording controls and a transcript panel.
showcase.imageCaption: Published workspace preview · may differ from the downloadable version.

scenes.imageAlt: SpeakFlow showing its active Listening state, recording waveform and dictation model.
scenes.imageCaption: Dictation in progress · actual interface with simulated recording; no microphone or private audio used.

scenes.imageAlt: SpeakFlow with the cloud GLM-ASR engine selected in the Dictation model control.
scenes.imageCaption: Cloud recognition selected · actual model selector with a demo backend; no cloud request made.

scenes.imageAlt: SpeakFlow displaying rewritten text and the original draft for comparison.
scenes.imageCaption: Rewriting example · original and polished demo text in the actual interface.

page.summary: Hold a hotkey, speak, release. SpeakFlow types your words straight into the app you're using. Run recognition on your own PC with downloadable local models, or connect a cloud engine. When you want more, add AI polish, translation and a voice assistant.

sections.title: Three steps to your first dictation.
sections.intro: Basic local dictation works without any AI account.

items.title: Install
items.text: Download the Windows installer. When you choose a local engine, its runtime downloads inside the app; no Python or build tools needed.

items.title: Choose an engine
items.text: Open Settings, pick your microphone, then download a local model or add a cloud API key and region.

items.title: Speak
items.text: Focus the app you want to type into, hold F2, speak, then release. Change the hotkey or switch to toggle recording in Settings.

sections.title: More than dictation.
sections.intro: Everything beyond the hotkey is optional, and each piece can be switched on when you need it.

items.title: Dictation & translation
items.text: Type into the active app with a hotkey, and optionally translate into your chosen language as you go.

items.title: Live subtitles
items.text: Follow local recognition in a floating window, with committed text and a preview that revises as you speak.

items.title: AI polish
items.text: Rewrite with your own instructions. Auto mode can keep your original wording when polishing isn’t needed.

items.title: Voice & selection assistants
items.text: Ask questions, rewrite, translate, explain or search, optionally including the current app, selected text or a screenshot.

items.title: Personalisation
items.text: Add hotwords, set rules per app, and let SpeakFlow learn from the spelling corrections you make after dictating.

items.title: Local history
items.text: Opt in to search, export, delete or re-polish past text. Turn on audio saving to re-transcribe it later.

sections.title: Pick the engine that fits.
sections.intro: Local models run on Windows without WSL and use your GPU when available. Models download once and are cached.

rows: About 2.41 GB · English and 13 other languages
About 2.48 GB · native streaming with language hints
Needs an API key and region
Needs an API key, region and model

sections.title: You decide where your words go.
sections.intro: Nothing leaves your PC unless you turn on a feature that needs it.

rows: Audio is processed on your PC. Model downloads need a network connection.
Audio is sent to the recognition provider you choose.
Text and instructions go to the services you configure. Screenshot, selection and search context only when enabled.
Both are off by default and stored locally when you turn them on.

requirements: Local models download separately, from about 730 MB to 2.8 GB
Cloud engines and AI features need your own API key or a supported account
page.note: The installer is not code-signed yet, so Windows may show a SmartScreen prompt. Feature descriptions follow the project’s current documentation; check the release notes for what each version includes.

name: Cinder
description: Your coding-agent usage stats, on your desktop.

showcase.headline: See where your agent usage goes.
showcase.intro: Cinder brings your coding-agent activity into one desktop view. Explore requests, tokens, and available cost estimates from local logs instead of piecing them together across tools.
features: Read coding-agent logs on your machine
showcase.imageAlt: Cinder's actual dashboard showing coding-agent usage, token totals, a model breakdown, and daily charts with demo data.
showcase.imageCaption: Actual Cinder interface · demo data, not personal usage.

page.summary: Cinder reads the session logs your coding agents already keep on this machine and turns them into one desktop dashboard: requests, tokens, estimated cost and quota pacing across every agent you use. Logs are parsed locally, with no network involved.

sections.title: One dashboard for every agent.
sections.intro: Click to narrow, compare against the last period, and export exactly what you’re looking at.

items.title: Filters that stack
items.text: Click an agent, then a model, and every panel narrows at once. The breadcrumb undoes each step with one click.

items.title: A chart with context
items.text: A dashed line shows the previous period of the same length. Hide an agent from its legend chip; long ranges bucket into weeks.

items.title: Breakdowns & CSV
items.text: Switch between Model, Day, Agent and Cache views. Every row is a filter, and CSV exports the dataset you’ve tailored.

items.title: Limits view
items.text: Burn-rate pacing, quota health badges from On Pace to Exhaustion Risk, pace markers and a depletion estimate.

items.title: Live updates
items.text: Cinder watches your log folders and refreshes the open window shortly after agents stop writing, at most once a minute.

items.title: Keyboard first
items.text: 1 to 4 switch between cost, tokens, requests and limits. R refreshes, S opens Settings and Esc closes a dialog.

sections.title: Works with the agents you use.
sections.intro: Agents that don’t log tokens or cost still appear: switch to the Requests metric to see them.

rows: Requests, tokens, cost, tool calls and models
Requests, tokens, tools and models; cost estimated
Requests, tokens, tools and models; cost estimated
Sessions, tokens, cost and tool calls
Requests, tools and sessions; API cost estimated
Requests, tokens, tools, sessions and models; cost estimated

sections.title: Set it once. Keep it current.
sections.intro: Open Settings from the header, or press S.

items.title: Update badge
items.text: When a newer release is published, an update badge appears in the header and on the Settings button.

items.title: Update in place
items.text: Update Now downloads the installer with live progress, updates Cinder in place and restarts it on the new version.

items.title: Your defaults
items.text: Choose the metric and date range Cinder opens with: Today, 7, 30 or 90 days.

items.title: Data sources
items.text: See every log folder and database Cinder reads, or trigger a full rescan.

requirements: At least one supported coding agent that writes logs on this PC
page.note: Costs are estimates when an agent doesn’t log them, and figures marked ≥ exclude some unpriced tokens.

description: Cinema, anime, books, manga and manhwa in one place.

page.summary: Everglow brings films, series, anime, books, manga and manhwa into one place. Find something to watch tonight, see what's airing, or pick up your next read, all in a desktop window of its own.

sections.title: Watch it. Read it. All here.
sections.intro: One app for tonight’s film, this season’s anime and the next chapter.

items.title: Cinema
items.text: Films and series, with Trending Now rows and a local Top 10 to help you pick something for tonight.

items.title: Anime
items.text: What’s airing and trending, with ratings, genres and a Watch Now button right up front.

items.title: MangaCelestia
items.text: Manga, manhwa and manhua with type filters and a Hot Updates row for what’s new.

items.title: Books
items.text: A separate books section for when you’d rather settle in with something longer.

sections.title: Made for the desktop.
sections.intro: A quiet window that gets out of the way of what you’re watching.

items.title: A window that hides
items.text: The title bar tucks away. Move to the top edge to reveal it, or press Ctrl+Shift+M for the menu. Prefer it pinned? There’s a setting.

items.title: Ads and trackers blocked
items.text: Layered ad and tracker blocking is on from the start. Pause or resume it from the Everglow menu.

items.title: Updates that wait
items.text: Updates download quietly in the background and only install when you choose Restart to update. Playback is never interrupted.

items.title: Remembers your window
items.text: Size and position come back next time, fitted to your screen even if a monitor was unplugged.

items.title: Full screen
items.text: Press F11 for full screen. The title bar stays hidden during video and full screen.

items.title: Easy recovery
items.text: If the connection drops while starting, a recovery screen offers Retry instead of a blank window.

requirements: An internet connection; the catalogue loads live
Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime, included with Windows
page.note: Blocking is strong but not identical to a privacy-focused browser, and some streaming sites may still behave differently. The Windows installer is not code-signed, so Windows may show a SmartScreen prompt.
